Back in reddit you could add tags to your username or to posts you submitted. Those tags depended on which subreddit you were on and were created by the moderators. They are called flair. For example, in AskScience you could tag your question adding flairs such as "Geology", "Biology", "Astronomy", etc. In sport-dedicated subreddits you could add a logo of a team to your username to indicate you support them. In computing subreddits you could add the kind of computer you were using as flair. This is a picture of a reddit thread with usernames with flair.

[web - flash] The Space Game - it's a defense game, in space, with more tightly integrated interdependancy

There aren't a ton of tower defense games which have enemies who do more than walk in a line on a path. There are games where the path is fixed, and there are games where you get to modify the path yourself, but there aren't many where the enemies have any kind of AI and where they're coming at you from all directions instead of just one. The games which do this tend to stick out. Maybe it's just because they're a little bit novel, comparatively, or maybe because they represent developers who are willing to put in a little more work.

Of those, Harvest: Massive Encounter is extra special for several reasons I think, but I don't want to talk too much about that here. It's a commercial game anyway, so not suitable for this sub.

Harvest came out in 2008, and about a year later The Space Game was released which is pretty clearly influenced by Harvest. Fortunately, The Space Game is free.

What it is: basically tower defense with only a small number of tower types. Instead of basing strategy around upgrades and getting the right timing for special abilities (I hate special abilities in tower defense games, they obviate the whole point), strategy here is all about carefully designing your interlinked space station. Making sure that your defenses don't have any holes, keeping your power grid operational and supplied, etc. It's good stuff.
